newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat Varadinska Banka plans listing, share split.
newsitem.headline: Croat Varadinska Banka plans listing, share split.

text.p: Croatian Varazdinska Banka, in which the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has a 10-percent stake, said on Thursday it would seek a full listing on the Zagreb Stock Exchange in the next 10 days.
"Our prospectus is just about ready, so listing in Zagreb is very near," president Mato Lukinic told Reuters.
Varazdinska would be the third stock to meet strict bourse criteria and gain access to the top segment after drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka were listed last year.
Lukinic said it might eventually follow in their steps and seek a foreign listing, though any such plans were still young.
Varazdinska is one of top five commercial banks in Croatia and 70 percent of its 332 million kuna stock is in private hands.
Its first issue shares had a face value of 16,000 kuna, but a 160:1 split was under consideration, Lukinic told a news conference.
"I hope our shareholders will accept this proposal, making the nominal value of shares 100 kuna," he said, adding that the move was sure to boost their already high market price.
One first issue share in Varazdinska was sold at 28,000 kuna on Thursday on the semi-regulated segment of Zagreb's bourse.
Its second issue shares fetched 1,050 kuna this week on a local over-the-counter market (OTC) in Varazdin, where trading is limited by very scarce supply.
Lukinic said the bank had been approached by several foreign investors seeking to buy up to 10 percent of its stock.
But it had no shares left in its own portfolio since selling 10 percent to the EBRD last October, Lukinic said.
"We also don't plan any new share issue just yet."
Varazdinska sees 1996 after-tax profit at 28.2 million kuna, 10 percent above plan and 48 percent up from 1995. It will pay 9.5 million kuna in dividend.
